investigator.note: We prioritised severe urban flooding and extreme rainfall due to Velachery's repeated history of deep inundation (including during Cyclone Michaung in 2023 and the 2015 floods) alongside wetland degradation, while also accounting for urban fire risks. For flood exposure and ecosystem changes, we evaluated low-lying population risk, walking access to tall flood refuges, and 2016–2025 land cover changes across nearby water bodies like Pallikaranai Marsh. For emergency response and animal readiness, we checked pedestrian accessibility to major hospitals, fire stations, and veterinary facilities across the area's 75 blocks.

report.summary: Velachery faces severe flood risks, with 104,098 residents in flood-prone blocks and 51,003 residents lacking flood refuge within 300 meters. The area also suffers from shrinking natural water bodies and zero veterinary facilities within a 2 km walking distance. Priority must be given to establishing designated flood refuges and emergency response access in high-risk residential blocks.

calamities.what_happened: During Cyclone Michaung, most residential neighbourhoods in Velachery had about four feet of water and residents were forced to evacuate; they said little had changed since 2015.
Inter-agency situation report: Velachery and Perungudi were among areas still underwater five days after Cyclone Michaung.
Velachery, Pallikaranai and Thoraipakkam were among the worst-hit areas in the December 2015 Chennai floods; reporters cite experts linking this to wetlands converted to real estate.
Report on continued filling of the Pallikaranai marsh for construction after the 2015 floods.
182 mm of rain in one day at this location (CHIRPS satellite-gauge estimate).

readiness.why_it_matters_here: Velachery has 51 flood-prone blocks housing 104,098 residents, with 32 low-lying blocks and widespread historical inundation during extreme weather events.

matrix.finding: There are 51,003 residents across 25 flood-prone blocks without a tall building refuge within 300 meters.
Only 56.8% of residents are within 500 meters of a tall building refuge, with median walk distance to flood refuges being 450 meters.
Major hospital access is limited during floods, with only 5.4% of residents within 500 meters walking distance and a median walk of 1550 meters (up to 2863 meters in Venus Colony).
There are 0 veterinary facilities or animal shelters in the entire area, with 0% of residents within 2 km walking distance.
No dataset available for animal evacuation or rescue operations during flood events.
No dataset available for post-flood veterinary care or lost animal management.
Water cover decreased from 4.7% in 2016 to 4.2% in 2025 (-0.5 percentage points), while tree cover decreased from 5.0% to 4.4% (-0.6 percentage points). Built area increased from 88.0% to 89.3%.
No dataset available for real-time natural buffer performance during storm events.
No dataset available for post-flood ecosystem recovery monitoring.

recommendations.what: Establish vertical flood shelters and safe evacuation points in unserviced flood-prone blocks.
recommendations.where: Bhuvaneswary Nagar, Venus Colony, and 23 other gap hex blocks
recommendations.why: There are 51,003 residents in 25 flood-prone blocks without an accessible elevated refuge within 300 meters, and maximum walk distances reach 1929 meters in Bhuvaneswary Nagar.

recommendations.what: Improve medical emergency access routes and pre-position mobile emergency medical units prior to storm events.
recommendations.where: Venus Colony, Udhayam Nagar, and Bhuvaneswary Nagar
recommendations.why: Only 5.4% of residents live within 500 meters of a major hospital, with median walk distance at 1550 meters and worst-case distances reaching 2863 meters in Venus Colony.

recommendations.what: Protect and restore local wetland habitats and water bodies to retain drainage capacity.
recommendations.where: Pallikaranai Marsh, Anna Nedumchalai Lake, and Kallu Kuttai Lake
recommendations.why: Water coverage shrank from 4.7% in 2016 to 4.2% in 2025 while built-up land expanded from 88.0% to 89.3%, worsening urban flood vulnerability.
